Do Now: Packets (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a packet need parts other than the payload?Show the answer

The payload is the data. The other parts say where it is going, its order, and how to check it arrived whole.

From Lesson 1. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2026, Question 3(e)(i). Each packet of data is divided into three parts. One part is the payload.

steps.label: Do Now: Serial Simplex (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: Serial Simplex (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do we need two words, serial AND simplex?Show the answer

Serial says how many bits go at a time. Simplex says which way the data goes. They answer different questions.

From Lesson 2. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2025, Question 6(c)(ii). The data for an alert is sent using serial simplex data transmission.

Total: 2 marks

steps.label: USB
steps.content:
2.1 Data Transmission

USB

Year 10

  • Today: what USB is, how it sends data, and why we use it.
  • You already know: serial, parallel, simplex and duplex. USB uses them.
Think → Pair → ShareWhy does almost every mouse, keyboard and phone use the same kind of plug?Show the answer

One standard plug works with almost every computer. People do not need a different cable for each device.

steps.label: What Is USB?
steps.content:
What Is USB?

Think → Pair → SharePredict: USB means Universal Serial Bus. From last lesson, what does serial tell you about how USB sends data?Show the worked answer

Serial: one bit at a time, one after another, down one wire.

So the bits cannot skew. They arrive in order.

  • USB is a standard interface: a way to connect a device (like a mouse) to a computer.
  • A USB cable carries data and power.
  • USB sends data by serial transmission: one bit at a time.
  • USB is half-duplex: both directions, but one direction at a time.
  • When you plug a device in, the computer detects it and loads its driver (the program that lets the computer use the device).

steps.label: Exam Question: The USB Interface (1 of 2)
steps.content:
Exam Question: The USB Interface (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the word "universal" matter here?Show the answer

Universal means it is a standard. The same connection works with many different devices.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2026, Question 3(c)(i). A drone can be connected to a computer using a universal serial bus (USB) interface to transfer the video recorded by its camera.

items.prompt: State what is meant by a USB interface. [1]
items.modelAnswer: A standard (universal) connection / port used to connect a device (peripheral) to a computer, so data can be sent between them.

steps.label: Exam Question: The USB Interface (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Exam Question: The USB Interface (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is "a way to connect" not enough for full marks here?Show the answer

The question says explain HOW. Say how the bits travel: serial, one at a time, and half-duplex.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2026, Question 3(c)(ii). A drone can be connected to a computer using a universal serial bus (USB) interface to transfer the video recorded by its camera.

items.prompt: Explain how a USB interface is used to transmit data. [3]
items.modelAnswer: Any three: the device is connected to the computer with a USB cable / port; the computer detects the device and loads its driver automatically; data is sent using serial transmission, one bit at a time; it is half-duplex, so data goes both ways but one way at a time.

steps.label: Activity 1: Half-Duplex
steps.content:
Activity 1: Half-Duplex

Think → Pair → ShareWhat happens when both sides try to send at once on a half-duplex link? Why?Show the answer

One side must wait. Half-duplex only lets data go one way at a time.

USB is half-duplex. Choose half-duplex and send data from A, then from B, then from both at once.

steps.label: Benefits and Drawbacks
steps.content:
Benefits and Drawbacks

Think → Pair → SharePredict: a new USB mouse works the moment you plug it in, with no battery. Which benefits does that show?Show the worked answer

It is detected automatically: the computer loads its driver for you.

The cable supplies power, so it needs no battery.

Benefits

  • A standard connection: it fits most devices.
  • Devices are detected automatically and the driver is loaded.
  • It can supply power to the device.
  • The plug only fits one way, so it is not damaged.
  • Serial, so the bits arrive in order.

Drawbacks

  • The cable can only be about 5 metres long.
  • It is slower than some other connections.
  • Very old versions may not work with new devices.

steps.label: Compare: Same Cable, Different Job
steps.content:
Compare: Same Cable, Different Job

Think → Pair → ShareBoth use a USB cable. Which one works well? Why does the other one have a problem?Show the answer

A works well: the mouse is close, and USB powers it.

B has a problem: 20 metres is far longer than a USB cable can be (about 5 metres).

A: a mouse on the desk

  • Distance: 1 metre
  • Needs power: yes
  • Sends: clicks and movement

B: a printer in another room

  • Distance: 20 metres
  • Has its own power plug
  • Sends: pages to print

steps.label: Exam Question: Type of Transmission
steps.content:
Exam Question: Type of Transmission

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can you answer this from the name alone?Show the answer

USB means Universal Serial Bus. The S tells you it is serial.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2021, Question 2(c)(ii). Julia uses a USB connection to transfer data onto her USB flash memory drive.

Total: 1 mark

steps.label: Exam Question: Two Benefits
steps.content:
Exam Question: Two Benefits

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must you not write "it is universal" here?Show the answer

The question already gives that benefit. You must give two OTHER benefits.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2021, Question 2(c)(i). One benefit of using a USB connection is that it is a universal connection.

items.prompt: State two other benefits of using a USB connection. [2]
items.modelAnswer: Any two: the device is detected automatically; the driver is loaded automatically; it can supply power to the device; it only fits one way, so it is not plugged in wrongly; it is backward compatible with older USB versions; it supports different transmission speeds.

steps.label: Exam Question: The USB Mouse
steps.content:
Exam Question: The USB Mouse

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does "less likely to arrive out of order" happen with USB?Show the answer

USB is serial. The bits go one after another, so they cannot skew.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2026, Question 4(c). An optical mouse is connected to a computer using a USB cable. One benefit is that bits of data are less likely to arrive out of order.

items.prompt: Give two other benefits of using the USB cable to connect the optical mouse to the computer. [2]
items.modelAnswer: Any two: the mouse is detected automatically / the driver is loaded automatically; the cable supplies power, so the mouse needs no battery; it is a universal / standard connection, so it fits most computers; it only fits one way.

steps.label: Exam Question: A Drawback
steps.content:
Exam Question: A Drawback

Think → Pair → ShareA mouse is used close to the computer. Why is the 5 metre cable limit still a drawback?Show the answer

The mouse can never be used further away than the cable reaches. A different connection could reach further.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2025, Question 5(c)(iii). A mouse is connected to a computer using a USB connection.

Total: 1 mark

steps.label: Activity 2: Why USB Is Serial
steps.content:
Activity 2: Why USB Is Serial

Think → Pair → ShareWhy did the long parallel cable get the letter wrong? Why does that make serial better for USB?Show the answer

Over a long cable, parallel bits skew and arrive out of step. Serial bits arrive in order, so the data is correct.

Send one letter down the long cable, first by serial, then by parallel. Compare what arrives.
